context: The current Active Prompt page displays status badges (Q, P, I) for Questionnaire, Plan, and Implementation. The user wants to replace these status badges with a smarter tab visibility approach where tabs are shown/hidden based on whether the corresponding files exist and the workflow has progressed to that stage. Additionally, the Modifications tab should only appear when the prompt has been executed.

questions.question-text: Should the tabs be clickable status indicators that also serve as navigation, or should they remain as standard tabs with visibility controlled by the workflow state?

options.label: Make tabs clickable status indicators with integrated navigation - clicking a visible tab switches to that tab's content
options.pros: Cleaner UI, combines status and navigation in one element, reduces clutter by removing separate status badges, more intuitive user experience
options.cons: Slightly more complex implementation, need to ensure proper visual feedback for both current tab and available tabs

options.label: Keep tabs as standard navigation elements but control their visibility based on workflow state
options.pros: Simpler implementation, clear separation of concerns, familiar tab behavior for users
options.cons: Tabs might appear/disappear during workflow which could be confusing if user is not expecting it

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A aligns better with the prompt's intention to replace status badges with tab visibility. It creates a unified UI element that serves both purposes (status indication and navigation), resulting in a cleaner and more intuitive interface. The title explicitly mentions 'statuses to be clickable' which suggests integrating status with the tab itself.

questions.question-text: What should be the visibility rules for each tab?

options.label: Prompt tab: always visible | Questionnaire tab: visible when questionnaire-generated=true | Plan tab: visible when plan-generated=true | Implementation tab: visible when implementation-completed=true | Modifications tab: visible when executed=true
options.pros: Directly reflects the workflow state flags, tabs appear as files are generated, users see progression clearly
options.cons: Questionnaire and Plan tabs disappear after implementation is complete, which might hide useful information

options.label: Prompt tab: always visible | Questionnaire tab: visible when questionnaire-generated=true (stays visible once generated) | Plan tab: visible when plan-generated=true (stays visible once generated) | Implementation tab: visible when implementation-completed=true (stays visible once completed) | Modifications tab: visible when executed=true
options.pros: Tabs remain visible once they appear, providing consistent access to all generated artifacts, users can review earlier stages
options.cons: Eventually all tabs will be visible, reducing the benefit of conditional visibility

options.label: Prompt tab: always visible | Questionnaire tab: visible when questionnaire-generated=true AND questionnaire-answered=false | Plan tab: visible when plan-generated=true AND implementation-completed=false | Implementation tab: always visible (or visible when any execution has occurred) | Modifications tab: visible when executed=true
options.pros: Hides tabs that are no longer relevant to current workflow stage, keeps UI clean and focused on current tasks
options.cons: Users cannot easily review completed questionnaires or plans without accessing file system directly

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option B provides the best balance between progressive disclosure and persistent access. It shows users the workflow progression by revealing tabs as they become available, while maintaining access to all generated artifacts. This aligns with the principle that once content is generated, it may be useful for reference throughout the prompt lifecycle.

questions.question-text: Should the status badges (Q, P, I) be completely removed or retained in some form alongside the tab visibility approach?

options.label: Remove status badges completely - tab visibility alone indicates status
options.pros: Cleaner UI, reduces visual clutter, tab presence/absence is a clear status indicator, aligns with the prompt's intention to use tabs as status indicators
options.cons: Slightly less explicit status information at a glance, users need to scan for tab presence

options.label: Keep minimal status indicators within the tabs themselves (e.g., icons or badges on tab labels)
options.pros: Provides additional visual feedback within tabs, can show completion state more explicitly, helpful for colorblind users
options.cons: Adds complexity, may clutter tab labels, somewhat redundant with tab visibility

options.label: Keep status badges but move them to a less prominent location or different format
options.pros: Maintains explicit status information, provides redundant status indication for clarity
options.cons: Defeats the purpose of using tabs as status indicators, continues UI clutter

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A is most aligned with the prompt's stated goal to 'instead of statuses... hide or show the tabs'. Removing the status badges entirely creates a cleaner UI where tab visibility itself serves as the status indicator. This is a more elegant solution that reduces visual clutter while maintaining clear workflow state communication.

questions.question-text: When a tab becomes visible for the first time, should it automatically become the active (selected) tab?

options.label: Yes - automatically switch to newly visible tabs to draw user attention to new content
options.pros: Ensures users notice new content immediately, provides natural workflow progression, reduces need for manual navigation
options.cons: May be disruptive if user is actively working in another tab, could cause confusion if automatic switching is unexpected

options.label: No - keep current tab active and let user manually switch to new tabs
options.pros: Less disruptive to user's current workflow, gives user full control over navigation, predictable behavior
options.cons: Users might not notice new tabs have appeared, may miss important generated content

options.label: Use visual indicators (e.g., badge, animation) to highlight new tabs without auto-switching
options.pros: Balances notification with user control, non-disruptive, clear visual feedback
options.cons: More complex to implement, requires additional UI elements

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option B respects user control and avoids disruptive automatic navigation. Since the execution workflow is typically done through VS Code with copilot (not through the Web UI), the user refreshes the page or navigates manually after execution. Automatic tab switching could be confusing. Keeping the current tab active provides predictable, non-surprising behavior.

questions.question-text: What should happen when the active/selected tab is the Prompt tab and a new tab becomes visible (e.g., Questionnaire appears after analyze mode)?

options.label: Stay on the Prompt tab - maintain current user context
options.pros: Consistent with Q4 option B recommendation, predictable behavior, user remains in control
options.cons: User must manually discover and navigate to new tabs

options.label: Switch to the newly appeared tab to guide workflow progression
options.pros: Helps guide user through workflow stages, ensures user sees newly generated content
options.cons: Could be disruptive, inconsistent with manual control philosophy

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A maintains consistency with the recommended approach in Q4 of giving users full control over navigation. The Web UI is primarily used for viewing and managing workflow state, not for interactive workflow execution, so automatic navigation is less beneficial and potentially more disruptive.
